title: "Category 4  Signal processing and deep-unfolded models"
description: "Turning classical iterative signal-processing algorithms into trainable network layers"
toc: true

<span id="top"></span>

Many classical signal-processing methods are **iterative optimisation algorithms**: a decomposition, reconstruction or filtering result is obtained by repeating a fixed update rule until convergence, using hyperparameters that are set once and applied to every signal. **Algorithm unrolling**, also called **deep unfolding**, rewrites a fixed number of iterations of such an algorithm as the layers of a neural network. The algorithm's update equations fix the network's architecture, so the model stays interpretable, while its hyperparameters become trainable weights, learned end to end from data instead of tuned once by hand.

This differs from the representation-learning projects in Category 2: there, a generic encoder learns a representation through a self-supervised pretext task. Here, the network architecture itself *is* a classical algorithm, truncated to a handful of layers and made learnable. The typical finding across the field is that a handful of unrolled, learned iterations matches or beats an algorithm run to full convergence with a fixed hyperparameter, at a fraction of the compute.

::: {.category-callout}
**A Master-level category**

Projects here require deriving and validating an unrolled version of a published iterative algorithm — graduate-level optimisation and signal processing. The Master bar is a new, justified design decision about what the unrolling makes learnable, not reproducing an existing unrolled method on a new dataset.
:::

## Learn first and find ideas

- General unrolling: Gregor & LeCun, [Learning Fast Approximations of Sparse Coding (LISTA)](https://icml.cc/Conferences/2010/papers/449.pdf), ICML 2010 — the founding example, unrolling ISTA. Monga, Li & Eldar, [Algorithm Unrolling](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.10557), IEEE SPM 2021 — the field's main survey. Yang, Sun, Li & Xu, [Deep ADMM-Net for Compressive Sensing MRI](http://papers.neurips.cc/paper/6406-deep-admm-net-for-compressive-sensing-mri.pdf), NeurIPS 2016 — unrolling a coupled, multi-variable ADMM iteration.
- Signal decomposition: Dragomiretskiy & Zosso, [Variational Mode Decomposition](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSP.2013.2288675), IEEE TSP 2014, with [reference Python code](https://github.com/vrcarva/vmdpy). Rehman & Aftab, [Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition](https://doi.org/10.1109/TSP.2019.2951223), IEEE TSP 2019.
- Ahmad, Wesemann, Waschkowski & Khalid, [Robust Spatiotemporal Forecasting Using Adaptive Deep-Unfolded VMD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00703), 2025, with [official code](https://github.com/OsamaAhmad369/MAGN) — the anchor paper, unrolling single-channel VMD.

## 4.1  Deep-unfolded multivariate VMD for correlated multichannel signals {#project-4-1}

::: {.project-meta}
<span class="meta-label">Task</span><span class="meta-value">Algorithm unrolling: a coupled multivariate optimisation algorithm rewritten as learnable layers, evaluated as decomposition and as a forecasting preprocessing module</span>
<span class="meta-label">Level</span><span class="meta-value">MSc only — no Bachelor variant is offered, see below</span>
<span class="meta-label">Compute</span><span class="meta-value">Light for the synthetic benchmark; moderate for the applied task (single 8+ GB consumer GPU)</span>
<span class="meta-label">Data</span><span class="meta-value">Synthetic multichannel benchmark (required) plus [LargeST](https://github.com/liuxu77/LargeST) traffic forecasting; licence to be confirmed</span>
<span class="meta-label">Starting paper</span><span class="meta-value">Ahmad, Wesemann, Waschkowski & Khalid, [Adaptive Deep-Unfolded VMD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00703), 2025</span>
:::

::: {.project-intro}
**What you will do.** Variational Mode Decomposition splits a signal into band-limited modes by solving a constrained optimisation problem with ADMM. A 2025 paper unrolls that iteration into a small stack of learnable layers ("UVMD"), cutting decomposition time roughly 250-fold — but for a single channel at a time. Multivariate VMD already extends classical VMD to couple channels through one *shared* centre frequency per mode. No deep-unfolded version of that coupled algorithm exists. You will design one.
:::

**Project goal.** Unroll MVMD's cross-channel frequency-coupling step into a learnable module that keeps the coupling genuine — rather than collapsing back into independent per-channel UVMD — and test whether coupling correlated channels, with the coupling weights themselves learnable, improves decomposition accuracy, noise robustness and downstream task performance.

**Data.** **Required:** a synthetic multichannel benchmark with known ground-truth modes, centre frequencies and channel counts (2–32) at varied SNR, following the validation protocol of the VMD and MVMD papers — the algorithm-design claims rest on this. **Required applied task:** [LargeST](https://github.com/liuxu77/LargeST) traffic forecasting (up to 8,600 California sensors; also on [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/liuxu77/largest)), the anchor paper's own benchmark — confirm its licence before allocation. **Optional generalisation check:** the [CTU-UHB Intrapartum Cardiotocography Database](https://physionet.org/content/ctu-uhb-ctgdb/1.0.0/) (PhysioNet, open, non-commercial, 552 recordings), the bivariate application MVMD's own paper used.

**Methods and code.** Start from the anchor paper's [official UVMD implementation](https://github.com/OsamaAhmad369/MAGN) — both the baseline to beat and the single-channel building block to extend. Use [vmdpy](https://github.com/vrcarva/vmdpy) as a numerically clean classical reference for validating each unrolled layer. No Python port of classical MVMD exists; porting the official [MATLAB implementation](https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/fileexchange/72814-multivariate-variational-mode-decomposition) is a well-scoped first task and doubles as the classical baseline.

**Baselines and evaluation.** Classical MVMD run to convergence; classical single-channel VMD applied per channel; UVMD applied per channel (the direct competitor); the proposed jointly unrolled MVMD; and an ablation with coupling present but channel weights fixed equal, to isolate whether coupling alone explains any gain. On synthetic data report per-mode reconstruction error, centre-frequency error against channel count and SNR, layers needed to match converged MVMD, and wall-clock time. On LargeST report MAE/RMSE/MAPE across horizons on at least two regions. At least three seeds for every learned method.

::: {.scope .scope-msc}
**Master research question.** **Does a jointly unrolled, learnably-weighted multivariate VMD recover shared oscillatory structure across correlated channels more accurately and more robustly to per-channel noise than either classical MVMD or independently-applied single-channel UVMD — and does that advantage survive into a downstream forecasting task?**

The minimum contribution is (1) a correctly implemented coupled unrolled update, verified not to silently collapse into independent per-channel UVMD, (2) a learnable channel-weighting mechanism in the coupling step, ablated against equal-weight pooling, and (3) the full baseline comparison on both the synthetic benchmark and LargeST. Reproducing the anchor paper's per-channel UVMD alone is a reproduction study, not the contribution.
:::

::: {.scope .scope-bsc}
**Why no Bachelor variant is offered.** The project requires porting classical MVMD from MATLAB to Python, deriving and unrolling a coupled ADMM iteration, proving that the coupling does not silently reduce to independent per-channel processing, and then making the channel weighting learnable. That is graduate-level convex optimisation and signal processing. A reduced version — port MVMD and unroll it with fixed coupling — sounds smaller but still requires deriving and validating the unrolled iteration, which is the genuinely hard part, so it is not a safe Bachelor fallback.
:::

**Practical notes.** Validate every unrolled layer against `vmdpy`'s classical update before adding any learning. Write an early test that would fail if the implementation reduced to independent per-channel UVMDs — for example, verify that one channel's output has a non-zero gradient with respect to another channel's input. The cross-channel coupling is the entire point of the project. Confirm LargeST's licence before committing to it; the synthetic benchmark plus CTU-UHB is a sufficient fallback. The anchor repository has no licence file — check with its authors before reusing its code beyond research and study.
